newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS END UP, FOLLOW U.S. MARKET SWINGS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS END UP, FOLLOW U.S. MARKET SWINGS.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed higher Wednesday as the market followed the volatile movements of U.S. Treasuries, with traders saying direction in coming days will continue to be decided by North American markets.

With the release of soft U.S. producer price and retail sales figures in the morning the market surged with U.S. Treasuries. But with the dollar softening through the session Argentine bonds fell back from from their highs.
Argentine bonds followed U.S. Treasuries higher again in the afternoon, as investors got more confident that the U.S. consumer prices report due out Thursday will confirm low inflation.
"The market continues to rise. The U.S. numbers continue to show that there is no inflation" which will lead the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave rates unchanged, said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was up 3/4 at 74. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.05 at 119.90.
Traders said the market was very difficult to call considering the volatility on Wall Street.
On the positive side, traders said, the market still looked firm. "Everybody is waiting for a correction but it is not coming," said another trader.
In the money market, one week peso BAIBOR, or the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, rose to 7.0625 percent from 6.9375 percent.
